about: BOSSES lane, 11/2/26 (rule 302, Paolo 11/2: 'Battle Brothers has unique locations and bosses with themes, I want that too... each time you kill a boss you get something that helps you interact with the city'). Act one's first three bosses, in the ladder's order (records/BOHEMIA_THE_BOSS_LADDER_v7_8_7_26.md rows 1-3). WORLD TWO's boss_map.json still owns the sign, where he stands and what falls with him; this file owns his PLACE (the landmark you see from afar), his RUMOUR (the feed), his FIGHT (the man, his gear, his crew, his board, his one lesson) and his VERB (the phone's button and what it does on the grid). Read by slices/bohemia_bosses.js. Every word is a draft:true attempt; every number is a shape TUNING owns. A modder adds a boss by adding a row whose 'n' matches a boss_map.json row. ROUND 2 (BOSSES 11/2, rule 330, ask lines 328 and 329: 'each one has to have their own aesthetic, and maybe a quest or two that leads up to them... I'm so confused by what that means'): boss.look is HIS OWN look on the people's rig (tools/bohemia_bosses_the_three_men.py); place.paint names his place's pictures painted in the map's own look (slices/boss_places/, tools/bohemia_bosses_paint_their_places_11_2_26.py), before and after; lead.asker is the person who lost something to him and asks for help (a mouth card on the road, CONTENT's card), lead.thing is the clue at his sign, read out by one of your men (it tells where he is and what he does to the valley); after is the person who tells you, the moment he falls, what his verb does in plain words and numbers; verb.button is the phone's one plain line and verb.tip what a held finger on it says; verb.first is what the map and the feed say the first time. BOSSES FIX 11/3 (rule 338, ask line 346: 'we still don't know what killing them does'): after.valley is the ONE line the one who asked says the moment he falls (what it means for the valley), after.take the button; verb.hand is the thing he hands you (his pot, his wrench, his filter: slices/boss_places/hand_<verb>.png, tools/bohemia_bosses_what_they_hand_you_11_3_26.py) with its one plain line (what, where, how often, the number), shown on her card and flown into the phone; verb.first.rise is the number that rises off your men where a verb is used. after.says stays as the long form (the held finger's). BOSSES 4 11/3 (rules 330, 337, 338, ask lines 328, 345, 346): THE BURN, THE SURVEYOR and THE CLIMB, assets first (his own model through the pipe: tools/bohemia_bosses_four_to_six_11_3_26.py; his place before and after: tools/bohemia_bosses_paint_four_to_six_11_3_26.py; the thing he hands you: tools/bohemia_bosses_what_they_hand_you_11_3_26.py run with four_to_six). Three new verbs, each its own kind of place so the phone's one button never hides another: burn (at night, on a dark block off a town, once a night; the fire stays and lights its blocks at night), survey (on a road, once a day: the fog lifts round you for good), climb (beside a tower, once a tower: the floors nobody reached pay batteries). verb.place_after is the small thing the verb leaves on the block (boss_places/<key>). BOSSES 11/8 (rule 437(a), ask lines 167, 346, 522: the first boss changes the map and the world around him, and it is real): 'ground' is the streets his crew holds round his place: every street block on the ring 'radius' blocks out from his door is shut by his crew's CHECKPOINT (slices/boss_places/<pic>_<x|y>_before/after, tools/bohemia_bosses_the_pots_ground_11_8_26.py) but his front (the way the sign points), so the map's own route goes round his ground; when he falls every checkpoint is shoved to the kerb and the walk goes through, 'till' batteries pay from what he held (Battle Brothers pays a big fight with what the place held), 'feed' is the strip's post ({where}, {streets}, {n}), 'mine' your company's ({till}), 'card' the one line under the thing he hands you. Kept with the game.

place.name: THE KITCHEN
place.seen: a black smoke stack over the strip, a copper pot on the roof

rumour.txt: Nobody eats on the strip unless THE POT says so. He has the last good pot, mijo. Ten men guard a saucepan.

boss.name: THE POT
boss.title: keeper of the last good pot

bosses.crew_word: THE POT AND HIS LINE COOKS
bosses.lesson: His cooks hold while he holds. He rallies them every turn he stands; drop the man with the lid and the line breaks.

verb.rule: anywhere on the open map, never inside a town; once a day (the pot needs the day to cool)
verb.says: Hot food on the block. The whole crew eats; they heal like a night's sleep.

feed.txt: Somebody is cooking on {where}. Real food. You can smell it from the freeway.

verb.tip: Your men eat hot and heal like a night's sleep. Once a day, anywhere outside a town.

first.feed: First hot meal. You cooked on {where}: your men got {healed} blood back, like a night's sleep. The pot cools for a day.
first.feed_none: First hot meal, on {where}. Nobody was hurt, so it only filled them up. The pot cools for a day.

verb.tip_cooling: The pot is cooling. You can cook again after a day.

hand.name: HIS POT
hand.line: COOK: once a day, anywhere outside a town. Your men get 8 hours of healing and no time passes.

asker.name: TÍA CARMEN
asker.from: a cook with no kitchen, sitting on the curb with an empty pot
asker.says: Mijo, wait. A man called THE POT took my kitchen on the strip. My stove, my pots, todo. Now nobody eats there unless they work for him. He put flyers up near here. Go read one, it says where he cooks.
asker.yes_says: Gracias. Look for the black smoke. That is his fire, burning day and night.
asker.no_says: Okay. The flyer is still up if you change your mind.

thing.head: THE FLYER
thing.what: a flyer stapled to a pole
thing.says: It says HOT FOOD. ASK FOR THE POT. Under it somebody wrote: only for his crew, the rest can starve. It points to the kitchen with the black smoke. His line cooks shut the streets round it with carts, only his front is open. I marked it.

after.name: TÍA CARMEN
after.from: back in her kitchen, the black fire out
after.says: You did it, mijo. His pot is yours now. Here is what it does: once a day, anywhere outside a town, press COOK on your phone. Your men eat hot and heal like a night's sleep, 8 hours of healing, and no time passes. Then the pot needs a day to cool.
after.valley: The kitchen is open again, mijo. The whole strip eats tonight, not only his crew.

bosses.tip: KILL HIM FIRST: HIS COOKS BREAK

feed.txt: The carts are off the streets on {where}. His line cooks ran with their aprons on. {streets} open, walk through, nobody stops you.
feed.txt_none: His line cooks ran off {where} with their aprons on. Nobody stops you there now.

ground.mine: His till was under the stove: +{till} batteries.
ground.card: HIS LINE COOKS RAN. {STREETS} OPEN ON THE MAP. HIS TILL: +{till} BATTERIES.
ground.card_none: HIS LINE COOKS RAN. HIS TILL: +{till} BATTERIES.
ground.note: draft:true. The radius, the till and every word are first attempts; TUNING owns 3 blocks and 30 batteries.

place.name: THE PUMP HOUSE
place.seen: a water tower on stilts, its valve wheel painted red

rumour.txt: THE TAP opens the pipe for who pays and shuts it on who don't. His boys sit up on the pipes with crossbows, bro. Don't run at them in the open.

boss.name: THE TAP
boss.title: the man with the valve key

bosses.crew_word: THE TAP AND HIS PIPE WATCHERS
bosses.lesson: His shooters hold the pipes. Stand off and they pick you apart; close the distance and they are only two men with bows.

verb.rule: on a water main: a street block beside the valley's water works (a pump station, a treatment plant, an intake, a reservoir) or a town's own gate; once per main
verb.says: The main runs. People bring jugs and pay what they can.

feed.txt: Water out of the main on {where}, free, nobody guarding it. Bring two jugs, hermana.

verb.tip: Opens a water main for good. People pay you 6 batteries. Works on a street next to the water works.

first.feed: First main opened. The water runs on {where} for good, and people paid you {paid} batteries.

hand.name: HIS WRENCH
hand.line: TURN THE WATER ON: on a street next to the water works. Each main runs for good and pays you 6 batteries, once.

asker.name: EL CHINO
asker.from: a kid carrying two empty water jugs
asker.says: Ey. THE TAP shut the water off on my street because we can't pay him. My abuela is drinking from the wash, bro. He sprays his name on the pipes. Find his tag. The pipe runs right to his pump house.
asker.yes_says: For real? Look for the water tower. He sits up there with his shooters.
asker.no_says: Okay. His tag is still on the pipe.

thing.head: THE TAG
thing.what: spray paint on a water pipe
thing.says: His tag on the pipe: THE TAP SAYS WHO DRINKS. This pipe runs to the pump house with the water tower. He sits there with shooters and the valve key. I marked it.

after.name: EL CHINO
after.from: at the pump house, filling both jugs
after.says: The water is running! Bro, you have his valve key now. Here is what it does: on a street next to the water works, press TURN THE WATER ON. That main runs for good, people bring jugs, and they pay you 6 batteries. Every main once.
after.valley: The water is running! My whole street drinks again, and nobody pays him for it.

bosses.tip: CLOSE IN FAST ON HIS SHOOTERS

place.name: THE SETTLING TANKS
place.seen: two round tanks glowing a sick green by the water works, a little stack

rumour.txt: The tanks by the water still make clean water. THE FILTER keeps the old plant robots walking. Mira: shoot the man, not the machines.

boss.name: THE FILTER
boss.title: the last man who knows the plant

bosses.crew_word: THE FILTER AND THE PLANT'S ROBOTS
bosses.lesson: He keeps the plant's robots walking. Kill the keeper and every machine of his drops where it stands.

verb.rule: beside open water (a wash, a basin, a lake, a reservoir, the springs) or on a main you opened; once per block
verb.says: Clean water. Every fresh wound in the crew closes two days sooner.

feed.txt: Clean water on {where}. Tested it myself. Boil it anyway, mija.

verb.tip: Every fresh wound in your crew heals 2 days faster. Works next to water or on a main you opened.

first.feed: First clean water, on {where}. {wounds} in your crew will heal 2 days faster.
first.feed_none: First clean water, on {where}. Nobody is wounded right now, so it does nothing yet. Next time a man is cut, clean water here heals him 2 days faster.

hand.name: HIS FILTER
hand.line: CLEAN THE WATER: next to water or a main you opened. Every fresh wound on your men heals 2 days faster. Once a spot.

asker.name: DOC REYES
asker.from: a street medic, out of clean bandages
asker.says: My patients' cuts go bad from dirty water. The last clean water comes from the settling tanks, and THE FILTER keeps it for himself with the plant's old robots. He talks on the radio. Find the radio and listen, you will know where he is.
asker.yes_says: Bueno. Shoot the man, not the machines. They only walk because he keeps them walking.
asker.no_says: The radio is still playing if you want it.

thing.head: THE RADIO
thing.what: a radio wired to a pole, still talking
thing.says: It's him on the radio: clean water, if you can get past THE FILTER. The signal comes from the green tanks by the water works. Kill him and his robots stop. I marked it.

after.name: DOC REYES
after.from: at the tanks, filling a bottle
after.says: The tanks run clean again, and his gear is yours. Here is what it does: next to any open water, or on a main you opened, press CLEAN THE WATER. Every fresh wound in your crew heals 2 days faster. Once for each spot.
after.valley: The tanks run clean. Clean water means cuts stop going bad, all over the valley.

bosses.tip: SHOOT THE MAN, NOT THE MACHINES

place.name: THE FUEL YARD
place.seen: two fuel tanks behind a berm and one big fire in the yard, black smoke

rumour.txt: THE BURN has every drop of fuel on this side. Only his people are warm at night. Mira, his axe takes two men at once, don't bunch up in front of him.

boss.name: THE BURN
boss.title: the man who decides who gets warm
boss.says: Warm costs. Everybody pays the Burn.

bosses.lesson: His fire axe swings through the three men in front of him at once. Never stand two in front of him; come at him from the sides.

verb.rule: at night, on a dark block (no power) outside a town; once a night; the fire burns for good and lights the blocks round it at night
verb.says: A fire on the block, burning for good. At night you see round it like in the day.

feed.txt: Somebody lit a fire on {where} and nobody is charging for it. Bring the kids, it's warm.

verb.tip: Lights a fire that burns for good. At night, 2 blocks round it, you see like in the day. Once a night, outside a town.

first.feed: First fire of your own, on {where}. It burns for good: at night, 2 blocks round it, you see like in the day.
first.rise: FIRE LIT: 2 BLOCKS SEEN AT NIGHT

verb.tip_cooling: You lit a fire tonight. Light another tomorrow night.

hand.name: HIS FUEL
hand.line: LIGHT A FIRE: once a night, outside a town. The fire burns for good, and 2 blocks round it you see at night like in the day.

asker.name: ABUELA PAZ
asker.from: an old woman wrapped in a blanket, a cold stove at her feet
asker.says: Mijo, a minute. THE BURN took all the fuel on this side. Now only his people are warm at night, and the cold takes the old ones first. He burns his name into doors. Find one, it points to his yard.
asker.yes_says: Look for the big fire behind the tanks. He keeps it going all night so everybody sees who has the heat. And his axe swings wide, mijo.
asker.no_says: Okay. His mark is still on the door.

thing.head: THE MARK
thing.what: a door with words burned into it
thing.says: Burned into the door with a torch: WARM IS THE BURN'S. The marks go toward the fuel yard with the big fire. He keeps the last fuel and sells the heat. I marked it.

after.name: ABUELA PAZ
after.from: at a burn barrel in the yard, warming her hands
after.says: You did it, mijo. His fuel is yours now. At night, on a dark block outside a town, press LIGHT A FIRE. It burns for good, and 2 blocks round it you see at night like in the day. Once a night.
after.valley: There are fires all down the street tonight. Nobody pays him to be warm anymore.

bosses.tip: NEVER TWO IN FRONT OF HIS AXE

place.name: THE SURVEY OFFICE
place.seen: an old county office with a survey tripod on its roof, one window lit

rumour.txt: 20 years I drove this valley and now I can't find a town without paying THE SURVEYOR for a piece of his map. His spotters sit up high, bro. Get to them first.

boss.name: THE SURVEYOR
boss.title: the man with the last complete map
boss.says: Every street has a price. I sell it by the piece.

bosses.lesson: His two spotters shoot from up high wherever the board has it, and up high a shot reaches farther and hits easier. Get to his spotters first, or keep a wall between you.

verb.rule: standing on a road (a freeway, the Strip, a big street); once a day; the fog lifts all round you for good
verb.says: You set his tripod on the road and fill in the map all round you.

feed.txt: Somebody is mapping the streets round {where} again. Real lines, no charge.

verb.tip: On a road, the fog lifts 10 blocks all round you, for good. Once a day.

first.feed: First survey, on {where}. {blocks} blocks came out of the fog for good. You can do it again tomorrow, on any road.

verb.tip_cooling: You surveyed today. Do it again tomorrow, on any road.

hand.name: HIS MAP
hand.line: FILL IN THE MAP: once a day, standing on a road. The fog lifts 10 blocks all round you, for good.

asker.name: MANNY
asker.from: a trucker with no truck, a torn road map in his hands
asker.says: Ey. 20 years I drove this valley. Now I can't find a town without paying THE SURVEYOR for a piece of his map. Ask the man at the bar, he knows where he works.
asker.yes_says: Gracias. He works out of the old county office, the one with the tripod on the roof.
asker.no_says: Okay. The man is still at the bar.

thing.head: THE MAN AT THE BAR
thing.what: a man at the bar who drew it on a napkin
thing.says: The man at the bar says THE SURVEYOR works out of the old county survey office, the tripod on the roof. He has the only full map of the valley and sells it a piece at a time. I marked it.

after.name: MANNY
after.from: at the survey office, copying the big map
after.says: You did it! His map is yours, and every town is on it now. On any road, press FILL IN THE MAP: the fog lifts 10 blocks all round you, for good. Once a day.
after.valley: The whole map is on the wall for anybody to copy. Every town is on it now, no charge.

place.name: THE HOIST
place.seen: a dead casino tower with a work hoist up its side, the cage parked at the top

rumour.txt: Everything good is up high, where nobody's been since the elevators died. THE CLIMB has the last hoist and only takes his crew. Careful, his hook on the chain reaches you from two steps away.

boss.name: THE CLIMB
boss.title: the man who decides who goes up

bosses.lesson: His hook on the chain reaches two tiles: he hits you before you reach him, the cut bleeds, and it can knock a weapon out of a hand. Close in on him fast, or shoot him.

verb.rule: on a street beside a tower (a casino, a resort, a high-rise); once a tower; the floors nobody reached pay batteries
verb.says: Your men climb the dead stairs to floors nobody reached since the power died.

feed.txt: Somebody got to the top floors on {where}. Lights up there for the first time in years.

verb.tip: Your men climb a tower to the floors nobody reached. 12 batteries, once a tower. Works next to a casino, a resort or a high-rise.

first.feed: First climb, on {where}. Your men reached floors nobody had touched and brought down {paid} batteries. Every tower once.

hand.name: HIS HOOK
hand.line: GO UP: next to a tower (a casino, a resort, a high-rise). Your men climb to the floors nobody reached and bring down 12 batteries. Once a tower.

asker.name: NENA
asker.from: a scavenger kid with a rope and an empty sack
asker.says: Ey, you. Everything good is up high, the floors nobody reached since the elevators died. THE CLIMB has the last hoist that runs and he only takes his crew. His flyers are on the poles by the casinos.
asker.yes_says: For real? Look for the tower with the cage on its side. He keeps the cage up top so nobody else gets it.
asker.no_says: Okay. His flyers are still up.

thing.head: THE FLYER
thing.what: a flyer taped to a light pole
thing.says: It says THE HOIST WORKS. THE CLIMB DECIDES WHO GOES UP. It shows the casino tower with the hoist up its side. He takes his own crew up and leaves everybody on the ground. I marked it.

after.name: NENA
after.from: at the bottom of the hoist, the cage come down
after.says: You did it! His hook is yours. Next to any tower, a casino, a resort, a high-rise, press GO UP. Your men climb to the floors nobody reached and bring down 12 batteries. Every tower once.
after.valley: The hoist runs for anybody now. The top floors are open, and the lights are on up there.

bosses.tip: CLOSE IN FAST: HIS HOOK REACHES TWO
